QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_21

question.text: A close-ended Cat III fund has total paid-in capital of INR 100 crore and has distributed a cumulative INR 145 crore to investors over the fund life. What is the DPI?

explanation.text: The Logic: DPI = Cumulative Distributions / Paid-in Capital = 145 / 100 = 1.45x. A DPI greater than 1 indicates that investors have received cumulative distributions exceeding the capital they paid in. The Trap: 0.69 inverts the ratio. 1.00 is the breakeven value. 2.45 incorrectly adds 1 to the ratio. Note: DPI + RVPI = TVPI until the final exit; DPI captures only the distributed portion of returns relative to paid-in capital.
